newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw Inc sees "robust growth" in '97.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw Inc sees "robust growth" in '97.

text.p: Laidlaw Inc said on Wednesday that it expects fiscal 1997 to be another year of "robust growth" for the Canadian waste and transportation giant.
Laidlaw earlier reported a profit of US$0.07 per share in the fourth quarter ended August 31, up from US$0.06 per share in the same period a year earlier.

"For fiscal 1997, we foresee another year of robust growth as we continue to build on the leadership positions we've built in each of our service businesses," Laidlaw chief executive James Bullock said in a statement. The results were slightly below analysts' forecasts of US$0.08 per share.
Fourth quarter revenues climbed to US$478.5 million from US$409.2 million a year earlier.
Over the entire year, revenues rose to US$2.3 billion in fiscal 1996 from US$1.7 billion in the previous fiscal year.

Profits for the year ended August 31 improved to US$0.55 per share from US$0.48 a share a year earlier. "Laidlaw's fiscal 1996 has been a year of substantial change as we continue to act on opportunities and react to market conditions in our various businesses," Bullock said.
He said a substantial part of a US$600 million gain on the sale of Laidlaw's solid waste unit will be recgonized in 1997.
Laidlaw recently sold its solid waste operations to Allied Waste Industries Inc for over US$1.6 billion. The deal is expected to close early in January.
Bullock said Laidlaw's environmental services segment continues to expand its revenue base but, like all companies in the industry, is beset by low pricing.
